ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In a three-dimensional Cartesian coordinate system, the positive direction of the $\mathbf{x}$-axis is horizontally to the right, and the positive direction of the y-axis is vertically upward. A uniform magnetic field is introduced into the system. A current-carrying conductor rod cd with mass $m=10\mathrm{g}$ and length $L=50\mathrm{cm}$ is horizontally suspended by two insulating strings of equal length in the positive direction of the $\mathbf{x}$-axis and remains stationary. The gravitational acceleration is $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. If the direction of the magnetic induction intensity is the same as the negative direction of the $\mathbf{z}$-axis and its magnitude is $B_{1}=1.0\mathrm{T}$, the tension in the thin wire is exactly zero. Determine the magnitude and direction of the current $I_1$ in cd.
2. If a current of magnitude $I_{2} = 0.40\,\mathrm{A}$ is passed through cd in the direction from c to d, and the magnetic induction is directed along the positive $\mathbf{z}$-axis with a magnitude $B_{2} = 1.0\,\mathrm{T}$, find the magnitude of the tension in the thin wire.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
0.2A, direction from c to d; do not add any other content
0.3N

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure gives three-dimensional coordinate axes, the y-axis is vertically upward, the x-axis is horizontally to the right, and the z-axis is obliquely downward to the left to indicate the spatial direction. The conducting rod cd is located on the side of the positive direction of the x-axis, rod cd is placed horizontally, c is on the left and d is on the right, so the direction from c to d is consistent with the +x direction; the conducting rod is suspended by two thin insulating strings above. Reasoning: First convert the data: m=10 g=0.010 kg, L=50 cm=0.50 m, so the gravity mg=0.010×10=0.10 N. A current-carrying straight wire in a uniform magnetic field is subject to an Ampere force, whose magnitude is F=BIL, because the direction of the conducting rod and the direction of the magnetic field are mutually perpendicular. 1. When B1=1.0 T and the direction is -z, the tension in the thin strings is zero and the conducting rod is stationary, so the Ampere force must be vertically upward and equal to the gravity mg. If the current direction is from c to d, namely along the +x direction, then according to the right-hand rule +x×(-z)=+y, the Ampere force is upward, which meets the requirement. Therefore I1=mg/(B1L)=0.10/(1.0×0.50)=0.20 A, with direction from c to d. 2. When I2=0.40 A and the direction is from c to d, namely along the +x direction, B2=1.0 T and is along the +z direction, then +x×(+z)=-y, and the Ampere force is vertically downward. Its magnitude is FB=I2B2L=0.40×1.0×0.50=0.20 N. When the conducting rod is stationary, the total upward tension of the thin strings must balance the gravity and the downward Ampere force, so T=mg+FB=0.10+0.20=0.30 N.
